public_rationale: The warning and the later OpenAI attack are documented. The incident records also identify consequential company-level choices and missing safeguards. They do not establish that Altman personally made the relevant decisions or that his actions were necessary to the attack. That leaves the sentence's central causal attribution unresolved rather than disproved.
limitations: OpenAI's own account may not fully establish executive responsibility.
A technical report's silence about Altman does not exonerate him.
A weaker claim about institutional responsibility would require a different contract.

statement.document_title: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands

from_speaker: he made sure that was the case
our_interpretation: He refers to Sam Altman and his early-2023 warning about offensive cyberattacks.
The immediate context identifies the July 2026 Hugging Face attack as the event that fulfilled the warning.
Made sure is read as attributing consequential development or operational decisions to Altman; it need not imply that he personally ordered the attack.
Only because asserts more than general executive responsibility: Altman's actions must be shown to have been necessary to the claimed outcome.
The causal episode is July 2026, described in the post as two months earlier. The 2023 warning is background.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish the attack and connect identifiable Altman decisions to its occurrence, with evidence supporting the claim that it would not have happened without those decisions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that the attributed decisions were not Altman's, or that the relevant attack occurred independently of the causal role assigned to him.
